newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer amid U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer amid U.S. gains.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened firmer in moderately active trade on Wednesday with the market taking much of its direction from gains in U.S. fixed-income markets, dealers said.

"I don't think it's really anything more than the fact that the U.S. is up a couple of ticks, though WI sixes (six-month when-issued T-bills) look like they're getting squeezed," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 2.94 percent from 2.95 percent at Tuesday's close.
"Our currency is marginally better but it's not really relevant; we're pretty rangebound all in all," the dealer said.
Dealers said activity was moderate and interest by accounts was light.

"I've been talking to clients this morning and everyone is a little confused as to why we're here," said one Toronto-based corporate dealer. "We're going to see a very choppy, very thin market until the FOMC meeting."
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield of 3.24 percent from 3.29 percent. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.82 percent from 3.83 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 2.95 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
